basis: Developmental impairment; dental defects 3/3, ptosis 3/3, skeletal dysplasia/osteopenia in evaluated patients (1/1); hypertriglyceridemia omitted at cap.
Microcephaly with intellectual disability; thyroid dysfunction in 2-3/5 and hypoparathyroidism in 2/2 support endocrine involvement; celiac disease is separate.
Cutis laxa with defining neurologic and cardiovascular disease; hip dislocation 2/3 supports skeletal involvement. Entropion 2/3 and cataract 1/3 omitted at cap.
Cerebellar atrophy and developmental impairment affect 30/30; hypotonia and motor dysfunction are neurologic manifestations.
Immune-mediated choroidal inflammation and posterior uveitis; choroidal vessels are part of the affected eye.
Malignant germ cell tumor of the vagina, a reproductive organ outside the axes.
Malignancy occupying the colon; lymphoma is only one subtype and does not define the umbrella.
Transplantable murine mammary carcinoma, not a human disease; its breast origin lies outside the axes.
Vestibulocerebellar ataxia; diplopia, nystagmus and vertigo reflect central dysfunction rather than direct eye or ear damage.
Carcinosarcoma arises in the uterine corpus, a reproductive organ outside the axes.
Congenital atresia of pulmonary veins is a vascular defect; pulmonary congestion alone does not establish lasting lung damage.
Neurodevelopmental impairment; strabismus 4/6 supports ocular involvement. Reflux and infections are separate diagnoses; common skeletal damage is not established.
Muscle glycolysis defect with rhabdomyolysis; chronic psoriasiform skin lesions occur in 30-79%. Kidney injury occurs in only 5-29%.
Congenital structural deformity of the talus and foot.
Hereditary colorectal cancer susceptibility has a gastrointestinal target; susceptibility alone does not establish an existing tumor or additional organ damage.
Intestinal polyposis and multiple bony exostoses jointly define the syndrome.
Purine salvage disorder; neurologic dysfunction affects most patients across the spectrum, especially classic Lesch-Nyhan disease. Gout and stones are separate diagnoses.
Multiple liver cysts define the disease; renal cystic involvement is reported in 30-79% by HPO, although renal function is often preserved.
Muscular dystrophy; conduction disease ~60-80%, cataracts >50%, gastrointestinal dysmotility >50%. CNS and endocrine manifestations omitted at cap.
Carcinoma of ovarian or uterine reproductive tissue; neither site has an axis.
Lens abnormalities and skeletal dysplasia define WMS; thickened skin and cardiovascular structural abnormalities are each reported in 30-79%.
Oligodendroglial neoplasm arising in the brain.
Isolated spermatogenic failure and infertility; no endocrine dysfunction or other axis involvement is established.
Otic capsule remodeling causes conductive hearing loss; this is localized ear disease.
Mitochondrial disorder; hepatic steatosis 2/2 with liver injury 3/3, DIC 4/5, renal insufficiency 2/3. Seizures 2/5 omitted at cap; respiratory failure may be secondary.
